pull.title: feat(pr-checkpoint): spend fewer CodeRabbit reviews: none for small clean PRs, CLI checks for fixes
pull.body:
CodeRabbit spend ran ahead of its review limit: 107 review events in the 7 days to 2026-10-29, 4 of them rate limited (Dave's usage export). This PR spends fewer reviews: a small clean PR gets none, a Minor-only fix carries the earlier review to READY, and the budgets and capacity bands are tighter. It also enforces the PR checkpoint, which ran in warn mode since PR B. ## What changed - **Small-PR rule RS** (`scripts/github/pr-checkpoint.mjs`): a normal, steering or infra PR of 3 files or fewer and 30 added lines or fewer gets `none` when the CodeRabbit CLI run is clean, and one CodeRabbit round (`[1,0]`) when it found a Major or Critical or did not run. Rules R1-R4 and Dependabot still win. Constants, not config. - **Budgets and bands** (`review-router.config.json`): steering and infra `[1,2]` to `[1,1]`; r3 stays `[1,2]`. Capacity warns at 30 and is high at 40 (was 40 and 50). `reviews_7d_manual` is 107, dated 2026-10-29: the band is live now and goes stale after 2026-11-05. - **READY carry** (`scripts/github/review-status.mjs`): READY accepts an earlier CodeRabbit review (`coderabbitCarried: { from, deltaLines }`) when the newest review has only Minor or nitpick findings, the change since it is 30 lines or less (additions plus deletions, all files) and `ahead`, the router state names the head, the PR is not r3 or `risk:high`, no file matches `checkpoint.critical` or `checkpoint.parser` (renames included), the CodeRabbit status is not pending, and CI and the proof are green. Any unknown severity, missing input or failed read blocks the carry. No pre-PR stamp condition (Dave, decision c). - **Missing-review texts**: a draft says "run /pathway; do not request a review"; an unrouted head says "re-run the review-router workflow". Neither says "post @coderabbitai review". - **Opening ask** (ccv3-mods `pr-loop/model.ts`): waits 30 minutes (was 15) and never asks while the CodeRabbit status is pending. - **Enforce flip**: `checkpoint.enforce` is `true`. Spike S6 passed live on #217: label `review:coderabbit` at 00:22:23Z, ready at 00:22:25Z, CodeRabbit check started at 00:22:59Z. - **Gate fails closed outside a checkout** (`.claude/hooks/src/pre-pr-gate.ts`): a command that names `Rev4nchist/Continuous-Claude-v3` from a cwd with no usable `review-router.config.json` is now enforced (it was warn mode). Dave chose this before the flip. - **CLI review of fix commits** (`scripts/github/cr-fix.mjs`, new): reviews only the commits after the newest CodeRabbit PR review (`cr review --agent --committed --base-commit`) and prints `CLI fix review: .. clean|N major|N critical|incomplete`. The READY carry needs a clean line for the current head. It never passes `--use-credits`. When only this line is missing, the reason says to run `cr-fix.mjs`, not to request a PR review. A re-review study of 29 PRs (`.claudedocs/2026-10-30-coderabbit-rereview-study.md`) found 12 real Majors in later rounds, 6 added by fixes, and no fix commit ever reviewed by the CLI. - **Risk list**: `checkpoint.critical` adds `checkpoint-shapes.ts`, `pre-pr.mjs`, `safe-message.ts`, `prompt-text.ts` and `provision-roles.*`, where 6 of those Majors landed. A carry never applies to them. - **Carry delta counts the PR's own files only**, so a merge of main no longer blocks it. A compare of 300 files or more blocks. - **`/pathway` confirms its head on GitHub**: `applyPathway` posts a hidden `pathway-confirmed head= pathway=

` comment between the label and ready. The router treats a ready PR as a new checkpoint only with a marker for the head and the label's pathway. A hand "Ready for review" keeps the class-raised note (CodeRabbit round-3 Major on #217, deferred here). The mod's Lock B denies shell text that posts the marker. - Rules `pr-review-loop.md` and `coderabbit-cli.md`, and `.coderabbit.yaml` comments, describe the above: one PR review by default; at most 2 cloud rounds outside the risk list; read every finding before landing; billing facts (On demand, $50 cap, $0.25 per file; the CLI has its own hourly pool). ## Evidence Proof type: feature RED: `node --test scripts/github/pr-checkpoint.test.mjs scripts/github/review-router.test.mjs scripts/github/review-status.test.mjs scripts/github/pr-loop-sync.test.mjs` @ 2b51c197 ```text new tests on the unchanged source (base 2b51c197): pr-checkpoint + review-router: tests 185, pass 169, fail 16 (T2b, T3c, T8, PD1-PD12, T20b) review-status + pr-loop-sync: tests 225, pass 205, fail 20 (RC1-RC12, RC14, RC15, SV1-SV4, item-4 texts) npx vitest run src/__tests__/pre-pr-gate.test.ts: 3 failed | 92 passed (95) (D1, D2, D6) CLI fix review and risk list (on 81d7896f): tests 542, pass 528, fail 14 (cr-fix.mjs missing, T20, PE1, PE2, RC16-RC25) pathway marker and reason text (on cdfb9aae): tests 439, pass 432, fail 7 (TA3, TA3b, TA3c, TA4c, TA5, RC18b, router load); router CP10a-e fail on the old router ``` GREEN: `node --test scripts/github/review-status.test.mjs scripts/github/pr-loop-sync.test.mjs scripts/github/pr-checkpoint.test.mjs scripts/github/review-router.test.mjs scripts/github/pre-pr.test.mjs scripts/github/cr-fix.test.mjs scripts/mods/validate-mods.test.mjs scripts/rules/test/coderabbit-cli-content.test.mjs` @ 68cf693c ```text node --test (8 files): tests 575, pass 575, fail 0 claude plugin test .claude/plugins/ccv3-mods: 989 pass, 0 fail npx vitest run (.claude/hooks): 109 files, 2916 passed context-budget-guard --repo: 23512 chars (budget 23516); ondemand-index-check OK; rule-router probe 137/137 e2e pre-pr-gate.mjs, cwd C:\Users\dkhay, node ...\pr-checkpoint.mjs --confirm coderabbit --by dave: deny (75d6d032 dist: {}) e2e review-status.mjs --fixture, 6 scenarios: carry only with a clean CLI fix review line for the head e2e pre-pr-gate.mjs, cwd C:\Users\dkhay, gh pr ready 217 --repo Rev4nchist/Continuous-Claude-v3: deny ``` Artifacts: `.claude/cache/e2e/2026-10-30-prD-A-red.txt`, `-A-green.txt`, `-A-e2e.json`, `-B-red.txt`, `-B-green.txt`, `-B-e2e.json`, `-C-red.txt`, `-C-green.txt`, `-C-e2e.json`, `-E-red.txt`, `-E-green.txt`, `-E-e2e.json`, `-E-ratchets.txt`, `-F-red.txt`, `-F-green.txt`, `-F-green-plugin.txt`, `2026-10-30-prD-gate-selfconfirm.json`. ## Claude review round (before the CodeRabbit review) A review workflow (5 Sonnet reviewers, 1 Opus verifier) found 17 issues; 12 survived verification (`.claudedocs/2026-10-30-pr-d-review.md`, local). Fixed test-first in a6c8a519, 72ae46fa, 74e51fe9: - C3/C4: the gate fails closed for a self-confirm, or a command in a CCv3 checkout, when no config is readable. - C6/C7/C8: cr-fix stops on a checkout that is not the PR head; an incomplete run is stderr only; an unknown severity counts as major. - C9: pr_watch tells the model to run cr-fix, not post a review, where the carry applies. C11: cr-fix.mjs loads the review rules. C12: the marker lock covers gh write shapes, GraphQL mutations and --input. - C10 (Dave): the --use-credits risk list also counts router class r3. - 6c61385f merges main (#220); README conflict resolved. ## CodeRabbit round 1 (74e51fe9) 1 Minor (cr-fix must run after the push) and 1 nitpick (marker from any author) fixed in 68cf693c. Nitpick deferred: show carry blockers in review-status output (follow-up). CLI fix review: 74e51fe..68cf693 clean ## Moved or changed tests (none weakened) - Fixture migration to `R5_FILES` (4 files, 40 added lines): T2b, T12, T14, T16, T17, T32; `runB` default moves TB3, TB5-TB9 with no assertion change. - T3c and T8 values to `[1,1]`. T11 replaced by PD8 (bands 29/30/39/40). T2c replaced by PD10. T20b flips to `enforce: true`. - Test harness pins `reviews_7d_manual_date: null` where it already pinned the count (the live date is after the test clock). - review-status: two missing-review tests now give the head a router comment, so they still test the routed text. - Mod: A2, A2b, CW5 move to 30 minutes; `record()` default `appliedAt` moves to keep the first check 31 minutes after ready. - pre-pr-gate: seven warn-mode tests now serve an explicit `enforce:false` config; they test the stamp, not the mode. ## Scope not included - `.coderabbit.yaml` path instructions for `scripts/github/**` still say "READY fails closed". The carry keeps that: every blocker fails closed, and a carry needs a real review of an ancestor head. Left as an instruction for the reviewer. - "Extra round only after a Major" stays prose: `budgetSentence` reads no severity. Follow-up. - The `pathway-confirmed` marker is accepted from any author (/pathway posts as Dave's gh identity, so a bot-only rule cannot apply). Anyone with write access can also add labels, so the trust level is the same. A marker posted from a file (`gh pr comment -F`) gets past Lock B, the same residual risk as the `pathway.json` deny. - `coderabbit-guard.ts` (unregistered) still has `MAX_RUNS = 2`; the rule says to change it before it is registered. - `readCarry` was checked endpoint by endpoint and through `--fixture`, not on a live PR that lacks a head review. The first such PR is the live check. - Greptile re-enable (DW-83). - Review follow-ups: C1 a same-head draft and ready click replays an old pathway-confirmed marker (UI click only; enforce denies the shell form). C2 the carry ignores a CodeRabbit round that left only a summary comment (fails closed). C5 cr-fix reviews merge commits from main in its range. Model + harness: claude-opus-5-5 (orchestration, review fixes) and kraken agents via Claude Code. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_0162xu8DEEpfvvES38pSowf9 ## Summary by CodeRabbit ## Summary * **New Features** * Small PRs may skip a bot review when a clean CLI review is available. * Eligible Minor-only reviews can carry forward to a new PR revision when changes are small and required checks pass. * Pathway confirmation is required before a PR is marked ready. * **Bug Fixes** * Checkpoint enforcement is more consistent when configuration is unavailable, and commands that attempt to post pathway markers are blocked. * Opening review requests now wait 30 minutes and are suppressed while a CodeRabbit review is pending. * **Documentation** * Updated review guidance, timing, and billing rules.

app.description:
# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

# 🦉 What is GitGuardian?

GitGuardian Secrets Detection detects and fixes vulnerabilities in source code at every step of the software development lifecycle, covering 350+ types of secrets like API keys, database connection strings, private keys, certificates, and more. The platform’s policy engine enables security teams to monitor and enforce rules across their VCS, DevOps tools, and infrastructure-as-code configurations. Our automated remediation playbooks and collaboration features bring security and development teams together to resolve incidents fast and in full.

## 1. Scan your codebase for 350+ types of secrets
GitGuardian scans your GitHub repositories and raises alerts only for critical secrets, such as API keys or other credentials. At scale, GitGuardian’s detection algorithm has been battle-tested on over three years of activity in all public GitHub repositories – totaling over 1 billion scanned commits!

## 2. Quickly remediate your hard-coded secrets
If you ever experience a leak involving a credential, we have a complete remediation guide used by 100k+ developers each year. We’ll show you how to revoke the secret and remove it from your git history.

##  3. Prevent secrets from reaching GitHub
Install ggshield, the GitGuardian CLI, and add secrets detection to your local development workflow using pre-commit and pre-push git hooks integrations.

# 🙋‍♂️ FAQ

**What is your pricing?**
GitGuardian is free for teams under 25 developers and offers a 30-day trial for larger teams.

**How can I be sure that GitGuardian won’t raise too many false positives?**
We have scanned billions of commits, sent millions of alerts since 2018, and integrated each feedback to improve our algorithm. Our alerts currently receive 91% “true positive” feedback from developers.

**My repositories are private; why should I install automated secret detection?**
Imagine if there were a plain text file with all your credit card numbers inside, you wouldn’t put this file inside your company’s git repository. Secrets are just as sensitive and should be handled with special care.

**Is GitGuardian available to be installed on-premise?**
Yes, you can contact one of our security specialists to look over the possibility of installing GitGuardian on-premise on your repositories.

# ⚒️ Installation notes 

You should install GitGuardian directly through your [GitGuardian](https://dashboard.gitguardian.com/) workspace on the Integration settings page. 

So that you know, your GitHub organization or GitHub account can only be associated with a single GitGuardian workspace.

# 👋 Support

If you experience any difficulties or have any questions, please reach out to us by email ([support@gitguardian.com](mailto:support@gitguardian.com)).

scripts/github/review-router.mjs: 1
`205-205`: ** Trivial** · **Security & Privacy** · **Quick win** **`confirmedPathways` accepts a marker from any comment author (scripts/github/review-router.mjs:205).** The code never checks who wrote the comment. The comment on Lines 200-201 says this has the same trust level as adding a `review:*` label. That holds only if comments are limited to people with write access. On a public repository, any GitHub user can comment on a PR. That user can then post a marker for the current head. The next `ready_for_review` event resets `pclass` and drops the "Class raised" note, which the marker is meant to guard. Filter on `author_association` (`OWNER`, `MEMBER`, `COLLABORATOR`). The issue-comments API already returns this field. Add `author_association: 'OWNER'` to the `marked` fixture in `review-router.test.mjs`. Add one test with an untrusted author.
Proposed fix
```diff +const MARKER_AUTHORS = new Set(['OWNER', 'MEMBER', 'COLLABORATOR']); export function confirmedPathways(comments, head) { const want = String(head ?? '').toLowerCase(); - const found = (comments || []).map((c) => PATHWAY_MARKER_RE.exec(String(c?.body ?? ''))).filter((m) => m && m[1] === want); + const found = (comments || []) + .filter((c) => MARKER_AUTHORS.has(c?.author_association)) + .map((c) => PATHWAY_MARKER_RE.exec(String(c?.body ?? ''))) + .filter((m) => m && m[1] === want); return [...new Set(found.map((m) => m[2]))]; } ```
Update the doc comment on Lines 199-202 to match.

Update its doc comment to describe the author restriction, set author_association to OWNER on the marked fixture in review-router.test.mjs, and add a test showing an untrusted author’s marker is ignored. ```
scripts/github/review-status.mjs: 1
`1065-1067`: ** Trivial** · **Maintainability & Code Quality** · **Quick win** **Expose the carry blockers. Today the output hides why a carry failed.** `carriedReview` computes the full `carryBlockers` list. It then keeps only `cliOnly`. For every other blocker, the reason is the generic `NO_REVIEW_REASON`, which tells the author to post `@coderabbitai review`. Two consequences follow: - The author cannot see why the carry failed (31-line push, critical file, unmarked inline comment, and so on). - `readCarry` turns any failed `gh` read into `null` through `attempt`. A transient API error then sends the author to a paid PR review instead of a retry. Return the blockers from `carriedReview`. Put them in a separate result field, for example `coderabbitCarryBlockers`. Print them in the non-JSON output. Do not change the `reasons` strings, because `pr-loop-sync.test.mjs` and the pr-loop mod match on their prefixes.
Proposed change
```diff - return { carried, cliOnly: blocks.length > 0 && blocks.length === cliFixBlockers({ body, newest }, head).length }; + return { carried, blocks, cliOnly: blocks.length > 0 && blocks.length === cliFixBlockers({ body, newest }, head).length }; ``` ```diff coderabbitCarried = carryResult.carried; + coderabbitCarryBlockers = carryResult.blocks; ``` Declare `let coderabbitCarryBlockers = null;` next to `coderabbitCarried`. Add it to the returned object.

fix(review-router): count a pathway marker only from an owner, member or collaborator

CodeRabbit round 1 on #221. Any commenter could post a pathway-confirmed marker; the router now reads
it only when author_association is OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR (/pathway posts as Dave, OWNER). A
missing field fails closed. The rules now say to run cr-fix.mjs after the push, because cr-fix stops
when local HEAD is not the PR head.

_doc: classes: path globs per risk class. Only ** (any number of whole path segments, also zero), * (inside one segment) and ? are special.

A glob that starts with ! is an exclusion for that class (r3 excludes eval fixtures under .claude/skills/**/evals/**). Each path gets the first class that matches it, in this order: r3, infra, steering, docs.
A path that matches no class is normal. The PR class is the highest class of any path. risk:high is never set from paths: a person adds it.
deep_enabled false: steering, infra, high and r3 PRs get review:coderabbit + review:deep-held, not review:deep (spec 4.1, Apex billing D3).
greptile.credits_used_manual: Greptile credits used this period, an integer you edit by hand. null means unknown: the router skips the u1 and u2 steps and the ledger says so.
greptile.u1_used: at or above this count, a review:deep PR gets a warning in the router comment.
greptile.u2_used: at or above this count, only r3 PRs get review:deep. Other deep classes get the held labels. Needs deep_enabled true.

greptile.u3_date: on or after this date, a deep-class PR gets one credit-check line in the router comment, but only while credits_used_manual is null. A known count means the check is done, so no line.
greptile.notify_login: GitHub login named in the u1 and u3 lines. null means nobody is pinged.
budget: CodeRabbit PR reviews per class as [opening, extra after a Major] (pr-review-loop.md 'PR review budget per class'). Read by scripts/github/pr-checkpoint.mjs. A bare number is [n, 0].

checkpoint.critical: path globs of files whose PR gets Greptile too when it is available (pr-checkpoint.mjs rule R3). A PR that touches one never takes the READY carry (review-status.mjs). Extended 2026-10-30 with the files where a fix added a real Major (.claudedocs/2026-10-30-coderabbit-rereview-study.md section 4).
checkpoint.parser: path globs of hand-written lexer and parser guards. Their PR gets one CodeRabbit review and no loop (rule R2). Dave edits this list.

checkpoint.enforce: boolean, read by the pre-pr-gate hook from the checkout the session runs in. true (live since PR D, 2026-10-29): the checkpoint rules (non-draft create, shell gh pr ready, hand review: label, self-confirm, non-literal --repo) deny the command. false (warn mode): the same commands pass and log one warn row to guard-decisions.jsonl. Only a literal true enforces. The stamp rules are enforced in both modes.

coderabbit.reviews_7d_manual: CodeRabbit PR reviews in the last 7 days, an integer Dave sets from the free '@coderabbitai rate limit' reply or the dashboard CSV export. null means unknown and changes no rule. reviews_7d_manual_date: the day Dave read it. A count older than 7 days counts as unknown.
